title: A global model aggregation method for federated learning with controllable proportion of local models
assignee: University of Science and Technology Beijing USTB

pse.problem: Existing federated learning global model aggregation method loses historical state when a new global model is adopted, leading to potential performance degradation.
pse.solution_function: Design and propose a global model aggregation method for federated learning with controllable proportion of local models that retains historical state by blending current and previous global models.
pse.solution_structure: Involves n IoT local ends in the same working domain, each contributing data for model training. Each IoT local end generates a local model which is securely transmitted to a central aggregator.
pse.solution_implementation: The central aggregator calculates a weighted average of the received local models based on their respective contribution factors (e.g., sample size, quality). The new global model is then a linear combination of the current and previous global models according to a controlled proportion.
pse.effect: Preservation of historical state enables consistent performance in federated learning systems and prevents potential degradation caused by adopting poor-performing global models
